Which iPhone apps can save a record of daily weather in my calendar so I can look back months later? Distinguish a historical weather diary from a changing forecast display or subscribed weather feed, compare suitable options and cite official sources.
ChatGPT said:

The best match for your request is Weather Events – for Calendar by Dejal. It is specifically designed to save daily weather records as events in Apple Calendar, so you can open a date months or years later and see what the weather was like.

There are also good iPhone apps that maintain a permanent weather diary in their own calendar interface. The important distinction is whether you want the records inside Apple Calendar or simply want a reliable, date-by-date weather archive.

An important subtlety: a weather diary can preserve a forecast snapshot rather than the actual observed weather. For accurate historical records, you ideally want actual observations, historical weather data, or the ability to correct an entry afterward.

2. Best iPhone options compared

1. Weather Events – for Calendar

Best for Apple Calendar

Dejal Systems · Free download, subscription with 2-week trial

Creates all-day Apple Calendar events with weather emojis, high/low temperatures, and detailed notes. Records remain available for looking back over months and years. Supports different locations on different dates and manual corrections.

Limitation: Its weather entries are based on forecast data unless edited; they aren't automatically verified historical observations.

2. Past Weathers – Weather Log

Tsuyoshi Matsuoka · Free download

Saves daily weather data in its own calendar, including hourly conditions, temperatures, humidity, wind, and location. You can retrieve missed days using historical data going back to August 2021.

Limitation: It does not advertise writing entries to Apple Calendar. Recording is primarily a one-tap action, with optional daily reminders.

Automatically collects conditions throughout the day, up to hourly, and keeps a browsable calendar archive with personal notes, summaries, and data export.

Limitation: Records are stored locally in the app, not automatically in Apple Calendar or iCloud. You'll want to back up exported data.

3. A weather calendar that is not a historical diary

WeatherCal — useful, but different

Web-based service · Currently advertised as free

WeatherCal adds forecast summaries and alerts to Apple Calendar, Google Calendar, or Outlook. Its forecasts update automatically, as often as five times daily for today and tomorrow.

That makes it useful for planning, but its official documentation does not establish that it permanently preserves past weather records. It should not be treated as a historical diary without confirmation of its retention behavior.

Official WeatherCal website 
Weather forecasts, in your calendar

This also illustrates why subscribing to a weather calendar is not enough. Apple describes subscribed calendars as external, read-only calendars. The provider controls their content, so a past date appearing today does not guarantee it will still appear next year. 
Apple Support

4. Another option: Apple's Shortcuts app

You can build a daily automation that retrieves current weather and creates a dated event in a dedicated Apple Calendar called Weather History.

Apple documents weather retrieval in Shortcuts, time-based personal automations, and Calendar event creation. The combined workflow requires configuration rather than being a ready-made weather diary. 
Apple Support (AM)
+2

This offers a useful alternative if you want to avoid an ongoing third-party subscription. For example, each evening it could create an event titled ☀️ 22°C — Clear, with additional readings in the notes. It would preserve a snapshot taken at that time, not automatically reconstruct the day's full observed weather.

For your exact goal, I would start with Weather Events, provided your iPhone supports it. It is the clearest documented match for saving daily weather into Apple Calendar rather than merely displaying forecasts. If you care more about actual historical conditions than integration with Apple Calendar, I would choose Past Weathers instead.

The one question that most affects the choice is: Do you specifically want weather records to appear in Apple's built-in Calendar app alongside your appointments, or would a separate app with its own calendar view be equally good?
